- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.5–1.0% above true value).
- Underestimate during strong bullish sentiment (sentiment > 0.5) in early window; model lags in confirming upward momentum.
- Overreact to negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) by underestimating downside risk; model flattens too early.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overcorrects after strong rallies (e.g., 3–5 days post-peak), then undercorrects in subsequent days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate mid-term volatility; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 15–25.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Lag correction: if last 3 days show rising prices, model delays peak by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
